html:
The Central African Republic civil war began in December 2012, when the Séléka, a coalition of mainly Muslim rebel groups from the northeast, advanced on Bangui and took it in March 2013.

Séléka fighters looted and killed, and Christian and animist self-defence militias called anti-balaka rose against them, killing Muslims in turn. Most Muslims fled Bangui and the west of the country. French troops and then a United Nations force were sent in.

Elections in 2016 did not end the fighting, as armed groups held most of the land and its diamond and gold mines. From 2018 the government relied on Russian mercenaries. The war revived the old divide left by the slave raids of the north and displaced over a million people, many to Cameroon and Chad.
sum: The Central African Republic civil war began in December 2012, when the Séléka, a coalition of mainly Muslim rebel groups from the northeast, advanced on Bangui and took it in March 2013.
